newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nintendo sees no big impact from U.S. game sales.
newsitem.headline: Nintendo sees no big impact from U.S. game sales.

text.p: Japan's video game giant Nintendo Co Ltd said on Friday that booming demand for its new 64-bit video game players in the United States may not translate into an immediate sharp improvement in its business performance, a company official said on Friday.

"We don't think the increased popularity in the United States would have a dramatic impact on our business performance for now. It's not easy to boost our current production capacity of 500,000 units a month," a senior executive said.
The official added Nintendo was trying to see if it was possible to increase shipments to meet the soaring demand.

The official, however, could not say whether Nintendo would be able to ship enough of the N64 products to meet demand. N64, known as Nintendo 64 in Japan, boasts improved graphics and is faster than the the older system which uses 16-bit chips.
Nintendo initially planned to ship 1.4 million units to overseas markets by the end of March 1997, but its U.S. unit wants at least 1.5 million units by the Christmas season.

Nintendo's unit in the United States, Nintendo of America, said on Wednesday that its entire shipment of N64 video game machines, totalling 350,000 units, sold out at retail stores three days after the game's launch.

Nintendo launched the latest generation video game player in Japan on June 23 after several postponements. The launch heightens the battle for market share in the billion-dollar video game business between N64, Sony Corp's Playstation and Sega Enterprises Ltd's Saturn players.
Nintendo also plans to launch the new game player in Europe in March 1997. But the official declined to comment on if the company would be able to ship enough of the players to Europe.
He said that would depend on if and how much the company could raise production, and on the amount of shipments to the United States.
